locator: Artificial Analysis methodology, version and evaluation list
quote: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1.1 uses nine evaluations: GDPval-AA v2, tau3 Banking, Terminal-Bench v2.1, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond, and CritPt.

The current AA component weights are GDPval-AA v2 20%, tau3 Banking 14%, Terminal-Bench v2.1 16%, SciCode 8%, AA-LCR 6%, HLE 12%, GPQA Diamond 6%, CritPt 6%, Omniscience Accuracy 8%, and Omniscience Non-Hallucination 4%.
Artificial Analysis v4.1 upgraded GDPval to v2, Terminal-Bench Hard to Terminal-Bench v2.1, and tau2 Telecom to tau3 Banking, and removed IFBench because of saturation.
Artificial Analysis v4.1.1 changed grading for HLE, AA-LCR, and AA-Omniscience and used GPT-5.6 Luna medium for those grading updates.
Terminal-Bench 2.1 contains 89 tasks and introduced fixes for 28 of 89 tasks with continuous validation.
The official Terminal-Bench 2.1 repository requires five trials for leaderboard submissions and identifies the 89-task benchmark set.
The current tau benchmark leaderboard publishes banking and knowledge task results, but its leaderboard is a separate owner view from the comparable AA tau3 Banking matrix.
The Sierra tau benchmark repository documents the task and harness lineage that underlies the current tau3 Banking family name.
The Scale HLE leaderboard is the benchmark-owner source for Humanity's Last Exam; Artificial Analysis currently operationalizes a 2,158-question HLE component.
The SciCode official repository identifies SciCode as a scientific coding benchmark and evaluation project.
The GPQA paper defines graduate-level scientific question answering and provides the provenance for the GPQA Diamond task family.
AA-LCR is the Artificial Analysis long-context reasoning evaluation with 100 questions and seven document types.
The GDPval paper provides provenance for evaluating models on realistic knowledge-work tasks with human-work comparison.

The current DeepSWE extraction contains 21 Best cards; GPT-6 Astra is 74% plus or minus 3% at 6.52 dollars average cost, Gemini 3.8 Flash is 74% plus or minus 1% at 2.36 dollars, and GPT-5.6 Sol is 73% plus or minus 3% at 6.46 dollars.
The extracted DeepSWE roster includes Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, Grok 4.6, GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.7 Flash, and GLM-5.3 Flash.
The extracted DeepSWE roster also includes DeepSeek V4 Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, Qwen3.8 Max, Muse Spark 1.2, Claude Sonnet 5, DeepSeek V4 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash, GLM-5.2, and Gemini 3.5 Flash.
The Artificial Analysis model directory resolves one current first-party page per DeepSWE family, with effort-specific variants recorded in the v1.4 mapping.

The GPT-6 Astra xhigh first-party payload records Intelligence Index 60.9931, GDPval-AA v2 0.55279, tau3 Banking 0.430928, Terminal-Bench v2.1 0.891386, AA-LCR 0.74, and AA evaluation cost 2004.1186 dollars.
The GPT-6 Astra xhigh model summary reports Speed N/A, so no numeric speed value is published for that selected page.
The Gemini 3.8 Flash high payload records Intelligence Index 58.6792, GDPval-AA v2 0.522725, tau3 Banking 0.449485, Terminal-Bench v2.1 0.876404, AA-LCR 0.81, and AA evaluation cost 825.8333 dollars.
The Claude Opus 5 max payload records Intelligence Index 63.0532, GDPval-AA v2 0.66197, tau3 Banking 0.420619, Terminal-Bench v2.1 0.891386, AA-LCR 0.756667, and AA evaluation cost 3836.0545 dollars.

The v1.4 AA extraction has complete 21 of 21 coverage for GDPval-AA v2, tau3 Banking, Terminal-Bench v2.1, SciCode, AA-LCR, HLE, GPQA Diamond, CritPt, Omniscience Accuracy, Omniscience Non-Hallucination, Intelligence Index, and AA evaluation cost.
Numeric speed coverage is 20 of 21 because GPT-6 Astra is missing a numeric speed value; the v1.4 score drops Speed and preserves the missing value as null.
The v1.4 parser decodes the currentModel object from first-party page payloads instead of searching visible labels, preventing a benchmark version such as v2.1 from being read as a score.
The ValueRank v1.4 score retains 21 models, 13 zero-gap dimensions, and no neutral fills; Speed is the only dropped candidate dimension.
The current ValueRank top five are Gemini 3.8 Flash at 69.4, GLM-5.3 Flash at 65.6, GPT-5.6 Sol at 61.3, GPT-6 Astra at 61.0, and Grok 4.6 at 60.8.
The ValueRank cost composite averages the normalized Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index evaluation cost and normalized DeepSWE average cost per task, with lower composite cost treated as better.

Supplemental coverage is incomplete for fields such as MLCR, Harvey, APEX-Agents, MMMU-Pro, AnalystAgent, AutomationBench, EnterpriseOpsGym, ITBench SRE, and Briefcase, so those fields remain outside the primary score.
Legacy IFBench, Terminal-Bench Hard, and tau2 Telecom are not mixed into v1.4 because current Artificial Analysis v4.1.1 replaced those benchmark identities with current definitions.
The Artificial Analysis data API documents benchmark, pricing, performance, and time-series routes, but the v1.4 refresh uses public first-party pages without placing an API key in the repository.
LiveBench release 2026-06-25 exposes 23 objective tasks across seven categories, including an Instruction Following category.
The LiveBench Instruction Following category is defined by paraphrase, simplify, story_generation, and summarize; ValueRank averages those four official task values.
The pinned LiveBench cost table publishes Cost Per Successful Task, and the ValueRank view compares that field with the official Overall Score for 20 matched cohort rows.
The current rendered Terminal-Bench 4.0 leaderboard contains 14 official rows with resolution rate, uncertainty, release date, tokens, and cost.
Terminal-Bench 4.0 overlaps 11 of the 21 current ValueRank cohort models; the ten unmatched cohort names remain explicitly listed.
